inversion_quotes.english: Because motion does not exist prior to the goer, who would go where?
inversion_quotes.should_be: Because [the goer] does not exist prior to the going

reason: Covers MMK 2.17-25 and opening of ch.3 completely; slips: འགྲོ་བ rendered 'goer' at start, ལྡོག་པ as 'cease/returning', and the prior-existence clause of 2.22 reversed (goer/going swapped).
All nine wisdoms on the side rendered in order; one slip: འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་བྱེ་བ་ཕྲག་བརྒྱ (a billion Jambudvipas) garbled as a billion worlds of this continent. Notes are plain explanations.
Commentary on heart-invocation, three sattvas, Akshobhya in Abhirati and Takkiraja all present and accurate; only small choices (གནས་གཟུང་བ as taking of the seat).

inventions.quote: Without arising and perishing, / An entity does not exist.
Arising and perishing for the empty / Is not at all tenable.

reason: Source is the end of MMK ch.15 with commentary (svabhava, eternalism/annihilationism, middle way); the English renders a passage on arising and perishing (ch.21) instead. None of this side's text is present.

Two kinds of ripening with their bases, the four qualities concordant with the accumulations, first-bhumi resolve and ten great aspirations, all rendered accurately and in order to the break at བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཡོངས་སུ་.

Opening clause (desire grew even stronger, it is said) dropped; the schism analogy is distorted (he stayed indifferent to preventing the schism, not indifferent to avoid one). Rest, incl. gandharva triple-asking and term glosses, faithful.

Verse on purified conceptions, the two factors (remedy, freedom from faults) and the faults of envy, stinginess, laziness/lack of confidence all present; weak opening (ཕལ་ཆེར་དུབ་པས as 'mostly for the weary') and 'what perform the action' are loose.

inversion_quotes.english: "Having previously established the foundation of training" ... therefore, the foundation of training was established previously
inversion_quotes.should_be: the training rule had NOT previously been laid down ... therefore it had not previously been laid down

reason: Word glosses of the first half are accurate, but the fascicle-two lemma མ་བཅས (not laid down) is rendered as 'established' three times, reversing the argument about why no rule existed yet.
Verse-by-verse rendering of the whole side; slips: ཤེས་བྱ་ཤེས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར rendered as 'object does not exist without the consciousness', and the touch/emptiness verse is garbled but recoverable.

Ten-limbed yoga, Akshobhya/trident knowledge-holder, mahamudra, the four caste mudras, solitary/unmarried maiden or courtesan, equipoise of vajra and lotus all rendered accurately to the break at མཚན་.

Pramanavarttika verses on attachment to self rendered in order; opening half-line dropped, the 'reversed support of experience' verse is garbled, and 'regard something as mine' is an interpretive addition to the finger verse.

Both sets of four concordant qualities with their bases (Sudhana example, wilderness dwelling for shamatha/vipashyana/shila, sravakas who abandon bodhicitta) accurately rendered; correction pair {bzangs,bzang} handled silently.

inventions.quote: <note>The four mental aggregates: consciousness, feeling, perception, and formations</note>
that person [fails to understand] everything

reason: MMK 3.3-9 and 4.1-8 complete; མ་སྤངས་ལྟ་པོ (seer not separate from seeing) mis-rendered, the note misidentifies the four (MMK 3.7 means consciousness, contact, feeling, craving), and the final broken line is completed with an invented bracket.

inventions.quote: At that time,

reason: Time units (120 moments, 60, 30 with water-clock), the primordial-eon glosses and lexical notes through ཡི་གེ/སྦྱོར་བ all rendered accurately; 'At that time' renders the previous side's དེའི་ཚེ་ན.

Dream signs, samaya breach, clear light and the yuganaddha verse all present; the clause about the stainless yogi not perceiving the two is garbled into 'two types of yogis', and the empowerment sentence is loosened.

Opening clause (grasping by following [a single shape] is not seen) dropped; the Samkhya argument about the gunas, pradhana particles and the senses is otherwise present though stiff and partly garbled (the Madhava sentence).

inventions.quote: The purpose is to develop respect for the Vinaya

reason: Title, homage, opening verse and praise verse present; the dedicatory verse is garbled (ཡུལ་ལ་བསྟོད་པ་ཉམས་པས་ཡིད་ཀྱི་གགས as 'obstacles born from exhaustion'), 'purpose' (དགོས་པ) is the next side's word, and {D4114} appears in the English.
Vajragarbha's silence, doubt and hesitation gloss, Vimukticandra's renewed request and the alphabet simile all rendered accurately through 'the Tathagatas'.

MMK 5.2-4 verses with commentary (space before its characteristic, oil from sand, two-characteristics fault, elephant marks list) fully and accurately rendered; correction pair (glad,klad) handled silently.

inversion_quotes.english: "Great" refers to the ultimate truth. "Vajra" refers to the relative truth.
inversion_quotes.should_be: "Great" is the relative truth; "Vajra" is the ultimate truth

reason: Five-stage commentary otherwise complete and accurate, but the two truths are swapped in the gloss on Vajradhara, and Esukhia # collation marks appear four times in the English (#stages, #Vajradhara, #unimpeded, #all mandalas).

Vinaya as protector's protector, refuge and abode, the mango/bamboo verse and the heedless-monk commentary all present; the clause on worldly censure and praising intention, and བགོ་བཤའ, are loosely rendered.

Self-awareness conclusion, Vadavidhi authorship verse and the critique of 'consciousness arising from that object' all present; the verse line and the closing clause (ཡོད་པའི་རྫས་ continuing to the next side) are garbled, and the memory/inference argument is loosened.

inventions.quote: Even so, why does the wood not appear? If you say, "Because it is seized by that," no. Because it does not obscure it; ... Even so, the wood would be seen. If, when the killer is killed, Devadatta does not return, just as in that case, If you say it is the same here, The killer is not actually killed.

reason: Verses on sound, letter sequence, manifestation and momentary destruction rendered literally in order, but the first half-verse is dropped and the last eight lines translate the next side (and beyond: 'Devadatta', 'killer is not actually killed').

inversion_quotes.english: Those are fully capable of [proving] impermanence.
inversion_quotes.should_be: Those are not capable of [proving] impermanence

reason: End of Pramanasamuccaya ch.5 and opening jati verses of ch.6 are all present line for line, but many terse logic verses are garbled (ཚད་སྣང་ as 'appearance of valid cognition', pseudo-unestablished = pseudo-deficient) and one negation is reversed.
MMK 25.4-17a rendered verse by verse with correct logic (conditioned/dependent, light and darkness, neither entity nor non-entity) to the break at ཡོད་པར་མི་མངོན་.
Vinaya as both teacher and treatise, the contrasting Buddha/Dharma example and the closing verse (protector of the protector) are all rendered accurately and completely.
Completion stage, illusory and vajra bodies, the clear-light glosses, the subsequent-entry verse and the Vajramala ultimate mandala all present and accurate to the break at འོད་གསལ་བ་ལ་.

inventions.quote: Having made the nose sense-faculty empty, and from the transformation of the syllable placed there, Akashagarbha is transformed
Emptiness, Very-Emptiness, / The third, Great-Emptiness, / And the fourth, All-Emptiness

reason: Source discusses Vajrasattva pervading all, the ten non-virtuous actions known as clear light, cited verses on karma, and the completion-stage yogi's samaya; the English renders an unrelated passage on ear/nose faculties, Akashagarbha and the four emptinesses.

All glosses of the five stages (mngon byang, sgyu ma'i sku, 'od gsal, zung 'jug), the compiler/Vajrapani line, the three yogas, mandala, and the gtan tshigs/dam bca' pair are rendered faithfully; '#' collation marks leak into the English ('#stages', '#Vajradhara', '#unimpeded', '#all mandalas').

Verses on the cause of persistence (gnas rgyu) and support are rendered in order and broadly correctly, but the opening half-verse 'like the melted state of fire and copper' and 'then that is itself the cause' are missing; the 'until it meets the cause of destruction' verse is garbled.

Every lemma-gloss pair from bshams pa through the bum pa'i gru / rdza ma'i gru and the opening of ra rkyal is present in order with correct sense; only stylistic choices (e.g. 'well-nourished' for 'tshag rgyas').

inventions.quote: Having made both the vessel <term>sruva</term> and the ladle <term>sruc</term>

reason: Homa ladle measurements and the master's preparation follow the source closely; minor slips: snod/dbyig pa ('vessel and handle') labelled sruva/sruc, 'dag byed pa' rendered 'acting as a purifier', and 'sits' anticipates 'dug ste' on the next side.

inventions.quote: Is an untenable thought.

reason: Objections, the two verses on the tetralemmas of past/future limits and the four views about the Tathagata after nirvana are rendered accurately; the final 'untenable' completes 'bsam pa 'thad pa' with 'nyid mi 'gyur' from the next side.

All arguments (viruddhāvyabhicārin as doubtful reason, mtho yor example, fire/cold-touch objection, kṛtakatva objection) are present in order; the dialogue structure of 'ji ltar na mi 'gyur te ... zhe na' is muddled ('How could it not be? Because if one asks...') and the opening sentence is awkward, but meaning is recoverable.

inventions.quote: who taught it on Vulture Peak
The purpose is to develop respect

reason: Title, homage, and Vinaya-praise verse are rendered, but 'on Vulture Peak' has no counterpart in 'sangs rgyas 'dul ba'i gtso la phyag 'tshal', the second homage verse's 'yul la bstod pa nyams pas yid kyi gags' is loosely rendered, and '{D4114}' leaks into the English; 'dgos pa' (purpose) is from the next side.

Lemma glosses (nor can, tshong dpon, mā ṣa ka, rgyal rigs, rtsis mkhan, rkun ma/rku ba, rdzogs par bsnyen pa, etc.) are rendered correctly in order; the opening fragment completing the 'yul mi' gloss is dropped and 'dus gcig tu 'ang rnam grangs kyis' is loosely rendered.

inventions.quote: and pity. Aspiring for them to attain that result is the mind of love. Thus it is said: "He possesses a mind of benefit, happiness, pity, and love for all living beings and creatures."

reason: The three abandonments of killing, the two causes (nye bar len pa'i rgyu / 'byung bar byed pa'i rgyu) and the two desires are rendered accurately; the side ends at 'phan', but the English continues with the next side's 'snying brtse ba ... byams pa'i sems' and the repeated sutra quote.

End of the apoha chapter and colophon are correct and every verse line of the jāti section has a counterpart, but many lines are word-for-word and garbled ('expressed by this side' for phyogs 'dis, 'pseudo-diminished' for nyung ltar snang, 'The mark of the object is the pseudo-unestablished'), so the logic of the futile-rejoinder verses is hard to recover.

inventions.quote: Just as an mango grove is ruined by burning a bamboo thicket.
One will become an animal, like the Naga Elapatra.
the proscribed misdeeds ... are like the bamboo thicket

reason: The source is a Vinaya word-commentary (na smad pa, the uddāna 'rgyab mnyen', Śrāvastī, Jetavana, glosses of grong/grong rdal, phyi ma'i zas); the English is an unrelated passage on a bamboo fence and mango grove and the Nāga Elāpatra, with none of this side's content.

inventions.quote: How could there be something empty?

inversion_quotes.english: An entity with a personal inherent nature does not exist.
inversion_quotes.should_be: An entity lacking the inherent nature of phenomena does not exist.

reason: Change argument (youth/old, milk/curd) and the emptiness verse are faithful, but the opening commentary sentence turns 'without dharma-svabhāva' into 'with a personal inherent nature' and the second sentence adds 'personal'; the last verse line completes 'ya yod par ga la 'gyur' from the next side.

Cessation of the twelve links, the chapter-26 colophon, the two verses on views based on the former/later limits, the Sarvāsrava-saṃvara sutra citation and the opening refutation verse are all rendered faithfully; the 'Sabbāsava Sutta' note is a correct identification of the named sutra.

Axe rite, the four castes gloss, the pañcatva ('becoming the fifth' = death) note, the rain-stopping visualisation and the mandala obstacles are correct, but the side's final clause (Amitābha transforming into three-faced six-armed Hayagrīva in ālīḍha) is cut off at 'imagine—', and 'charnel-ground cloth' is reduced to '—tery'.

inventions.quote: should seek and inquire about

reason: Four distinctions of benefit, the refined-gold simile with three placements, rūpakāya/dharmakāya vision, three kinds of service and the first-bhūmi sutra line are rendered accurately; 'seek and inquire' (yongs su btsal/dri bar bya) comes from the next side.

Vimukticandra's point, the two kinds of certainty (rnam smin myong bar nges pa / las byed par nges pa), the letter/syllable/number/teaching/mātṛkā glosses, the two request verses to Vajragarbha and the realization/scripture analysis are rendered faithfully.

Every verse of this apoha section (tree/non-tree mutual dependence objection, convention by pointing, 'realizing as one', words like 'knowable') has a counterpart in order; several lines are literal and opaque ('nature of a limb that is entirely abandoned', 'This too is a tree and Only this'), but nothing is reversed or missing.

The Vinaya-as-teacher-and-treatise argument, the contrasting Buddha/Dharma example (distinct natures counted as one) and the three verse lines of the next stanza are rendered faithfully and stop where the side stops.

The heart-invocation sequence (preliminaries list, samaya/jñāna/samādhi-sattvas, heart seat on lotus and moon, Abhirati retinues, Ṭakkirāja) is rendered in order with correct sense; only 'taking of the seat' for gnas gzung ba is a slight slip.

inventions.quote: The word "also" is mentioned to differentiate this from the previous <term>avishesha-sama</term>
to show the pot as a <term>sadharmya-drstanta</term>

reason: Source refutes the Sāṃkhya inference of a single cause with shared genus (guṇas, sattva, pleasure from sound etc., puruṣa inferring three guṇas); the English is an unrelated passage on the jātis avisesa-sama/vikalpa-sama with the pot example, containing none of this side's content.

Svasaṃvedana as result, the Vādavidhi-not-by-Vasubandhu verse and gloss, the 'arising from that object' critique (all conditions vs. ālambana, smoke/fire, appearance vs. real cause, aggregates making the five saṃvṛti) are present; the verse opening is muddled and the final sentence on blue appearances and substances is garbled ('they also exist as substantial entities').

inventions.quote: <note>The four mental aggregates: consciousness, feeling, perception, and formations</note>
that person [fails to understand] everything

inversion_quotes.english: Without the act of seeing, the viewer does not exist; the same applies even if the act of seeing is abandoned.
inversion_quotes.should_be: There is no seer not separated from seeing, nor one separated from seeing.

reason: MMK 3.4-3.9 and 4.1-4.8 are all present and mostly accurate, but MMK 3.6's 'not separated (ma spangs)' is rendered 'without', collapsing the dilemma; the note on the 'four' (MMK 3.7: consciousness, contact, feeling, craving) is wrong; the final bracketed guess replaces 'has not answered' (lan btab min, next side).

inventions.quote: one posits and designates the existence of a "life-force"
The phrase "former canopies"
interest in eliminating existence, interest in desire, interest in conceptualization

reason: Source explains the kinds of knowledge (of causes, results, aims, means, wisdom, gathering, the perfections) with upāya/prajñā; the English is an unrelated passage on five faults regarding ultimate truth, 'former canopies' and disputing sectarians, with none of this side's content.

Two kinds of ripening with their bases (patience/gentleness, wilderness), the four bodhi-concordant qualities and their bases, the ten great aspirations and the four means of gathering are rendered accurately, ending where the side ends at brtson 'grus yongs su.

inversion_quotes.english: This is quite possible in a town, despite the many immediate distractions.
inversion_quotes.should_be: Not a town, because it has many immediate activities.

reason: Both sets of four bodhi-concordant qualities, the Sudhana example and the bases are rendered faithfully, but the sentence excluding the town as a basis for practice is reversed into an affirmation.

inversion_quotes.english: It is suitable to say that the motion and the goer are the same entity.
inversion_quotes.should_be: It is not suitable to say that the going and the goer are the same.

reason: MMK 2.14-2.25, the chapter-2 colophon and MMK 3.1-3.2 are all present and otherwise accurate, but MMK 2.18a 'byar mi rung' is rendered 'It is suitable', reversing Nāgārjuna's denial of identity of going and goer; 'goer' for 'gro ba in the first line is a minor slip.

inventions.quote: remains

reason: Three realms and four birth-types, support/supported examples, equality of body/speech/mind and the dissolution sequence (three syllables, Om Ah into Hum, Vajradhara with Sparśavajrā) are rendered faithfully; 'remains' anticipates 'gnas par bya' on the next side.
